questions.stem: A train travels in a straight line along a road covering a distance of $$ 45 \\text{ km} $$ in $$ 15 \\text{ minutes} $$. What is its average velocity, in $$ \\text{km/h} $$?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify given values.**
Distance ($$ d $$) = $$ 45 \\text{ km} $$
Time ($$ t $$) = $$ 15 \\text{ minutes} $$

**Step 2: Convert time to hours.**
$$ t = \\frac{15}{60} \\text{ hours} = 0.25 \\text{ h} $$

**Step 3: Apply the average velocity formula.**
$$ V_{avg} = \\frac{d}{t} $$
$$ V_{avg} = \\frac{45 \\text{ km}}{0.25 \\text{ h}} = 180 \\text{ km/h} $$

**Result:** 180 km/h

explanation_steps: In the CGS (Centimeter-Gram-Second) system of units, the fundamental unit for mass is the **gram**.

questions.stem: The dimensions of acceleration are
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Formula for acceleration.**
$$ a = \\frac{\\text{Velocity}}{\\text{Time}} $$

**Step 2: Find dimensions of components.**
Dimension of Velocity ($$ v $$) = $$ [LT^{-1}] $$
Dimension of Time ($$ t $$) = $$ [T] $$

**Step 3: Combine.**
$$ [a] = \\frac{[LT^{-1}]}{[T]} = [LT^{-1} \\cdot T^{-1}] = [LT^{-2}] $$

questions.stem: An object moves in circular motion with a constant speed of $$ 12 \\text{ m/s} $$. The velocity of the object is
explanation_steps: In uniform circular motion, while the **speed** is constant, the **velocity** (a vector) is always directed **tangent** to the circular path. A tangent line is always perpendicular to the radius at that point.

questions.stem: Displacements A and B, which are perpendicular to each other are acting on the same point of a body. If the magnitudes of A and B are, **respectively**, $$ 6 \\text{ m} $$ and $$ 8 \\text{ m} $$, the magnitude of the resultant displacement is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Use the Pythagorean theorem for perpendicular vectors.**
$$ R = \\sqrt{A^2 + B^2} $$

**Step 2: Plug in the values.**
$$ R = \\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} $$
$$ R = \\sqrt{36 + 64} $$
$$ R = \\sqrt{100} $$

**Step 3: Calculate the square root.**
$$ R = 10 \\text{ m} $$

**Result:** 10 m

questions.stem: If a car is moving at uniform speed of $$ 50 \\text{ km/h} $$, the speedometer needle of the car

options.A: deflects to the right on the scale.
options.B: stays at the same point on the scale.
options.C: deflects to the left and then to the right on the scale.
options.D: deflects to the left on the scale.
options.E: deflects to the right and then to the left on the scale.

explanation_steps: Uniform speed means the speed is constant over time. Therefore, the speedometer needle, which indicates instantaneous speed, will remain fixed at the same point ($$ 50 \\text{ km/h} $$).

questions.stem: A student of mass $$ 50 \\text{ kg} $$ is in an elevator accelerating with $$ 2 \\text{ m/s}^2 $$ upward. The apparent weight of the student, in newtons, is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Formula for apparent weight in an upward accelerating elevator.**
$$ W_{app} = m(g + a) $$

**Step 2: Plug in the given values.**
$$ m = 50 \\text{ kg} $$
$$ g = 10 \\text{ m/s}^2 $$ (from the constants table)
$$ a = 2 \\text{ m/s}^2 $$

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ W_{app} = 50(10 + 2) $$
$$ W_{app} = 50 \\times 12 = 600 \\text{ N} $$

**Result:** 600 N

questions.stem: In an inelastic collision the objects move in such a way that

options.E: other forms of energy are conserved.

explanation_steps: In all types of isolated collisions (elastic or inelastic), **momentum is always conserved**. However, in an **inelastic** collision, kinetic energy is NOT conserved (it is transformed into heat, sound, or deformation).

questions.stem: The efficiency of a $$ 1200 \\text{ W} $$ motor is $$ 75\% $$. The work done by the motor in $$ 0.5 \\text{ minutes} $$ is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate useful power output.**
$$ P_{out} = \\text{Efficiency} \\times P_{in} $$
$$ P_{out} = 0.75 \\times 1200 \\text{ W} = 900 \\text{ W} $$

**Step 2: Convert time to seconds.**
$$ t = 0.5 \\text{ minutes} = 30 \\text{ seconds} $$

**Step 3: Calculate work done.**
$$ W = P_{out} \\times t $$
$$ W = 900 \\text{ W} \\times 30 \\text{ s} = 27,000 \\text{ J} $$

**Result:** 27,000 J

questions.stem: A book of weight $$ 5 \\text{ N} $$ is placed on a desk. The reaction force to the weight of the book is a force of $$ 5 \\text{ N} $$ exerted by the
explanation_steps: According to **Newton's Third Law**, every action has an equal and opposite reaction. The 'weight' of the book is the Earth pulling the book down (Action: Earth on Book). The reaction is the book pulling the Earth up (Reaction: Book on Earth).

questions.stem: A teacher of mass $$ 64 \\text{ kg} $$ climbs to the top of a mountain in $$ 8 \\text{ seconds} $$, doing work at a rate of $$ 800 \\text{ W} $$. The height of the mountain, in meters, is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify given values.**
$$ m = 64 \\text{ kg} $$, $$ t = 8 \\text{ s} $$, $$ P = 800 \\text{ W} $$, $$ g = 10 \\text{ m/s}^2 $$

**Step 2: Use the power formula for vertical climbing.**
$$ P = \\frac{W}{t} = \\frac{mgh}{t} $$

**Step 3: Solve for height ($$ h $$).**
$$ 800 = \\frac{64 \\times 10 \\times h}{8} $$
$$ 800 = 80h $$
$$ h = \\frac{800}{80} = 10 \\text{ m} $$

**Result:** 10 m

questions.stem:
The distance-time graph for a car moving in a straight line is shown in **figure 1**. Which one of the following statements is **correct**?

![Diagram](file:///android_asset/exam_images/physics_2024_q12_1.webp)

options.A: The average velocity from A to B is $$ 15 \\text{ m/s} $$.
options.B: The average velocity from B to C is $$ 3 \\text{ m/s} $$.
options.C: The total distance covered from A to D is $$ 20 \\text{ m} $$.
options.D: The velocity of the car at point D is $$ 7.5 \\text{ m/s} $$.
options.E: The car is at rest from point B to point C for 3 seconds.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Analyze segment B to C.**
At point B, time is $$ 2 \\text{ s} $$ and distance is $$ 15 \\text{ m} $$. At point C, time is $$ 5 \\text{ s} $$ and distance is still $$ 15 \\text{ m} $$.

**Step 2: Check for motion.**
Since the distance does not change, the car is at rest. The duration is $$ 5 \\text{ s} - 2 \\text{ s} = 3 \\text{ s} $$.

**Step 3: Evaluate other options.**
- A: $$ V_{AB} = 15/2 = 7.5 \\text{ m/s} $$ (Incorrect).
- B: $$ V_{BC} = 0 $$ because distance is constant (Incorrect).
- C: Total distance = Distance to A-B ($$ 15 \\text{ m} $$) + Distance C-D ($$ 15 \\text{ m} $$) = $$ 30 \\text{ m} $$ (Incorrect).
- D: Point D is where it returns to 0, but the instantaneous velocity at that point (slope of CD) is $$ -15 \\text{ m/s} $$.

questions.stem: Hook's law states that work done on a stretch or compression of an elastic material is stored as energy in the material and is known as
explanation_steps: Energy stored in a body due to its deformation (stretching or compressing) is defined as **elastic potential energy**.

questions.stem: A $$ 5 \\text{ kg} $$ iron block is pulled by a force of $$ 12 \\text{ N} $$ acting at an angle of $$ 30^\\circ $$ with the horizontal placed on a frictionless horizontal surface. The normal force on the block, in newtons, is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify vertical forces.**
- Weight ($$ W = mg $$) acting down.
- Normal force ($$ N $$) acting up.
- Vertical component of pull ($$ F_y = F \sin 30^\\circ $$) acting up.

**Step 2: Apply equilibrium in the vertical direction ($$ ∑F_y = 0 $$).**
$$ N + F \sin 30^\\circ - mg = 0 $$
$$ N = mg - F \sin 30^\\circ $$

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ N = (5 \\times 10) - (12 \\times 0.5) $$
$$ N = 50 - 6 = 44 \\text{ N} $$

**Result:** 44 N

questions.stem: A heat engine undergoes a process in which it absorbs $$ 200 \\text{ cal} $$ of heat and at the same time $$ 500 \\text{ J} $$ of work is done on it. The change in internal energy of the engine during the process, in joules, is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Convert units.**
$$ Q = 200 \\text{ cal} \\times 4.2 \\text{ J/cal} = 840 \\text{ J} $$

**Step 2: Sign convention for work.**
Work done **on** the system is negative: $$ W = -500 \\text{ J} $$.

**Step 3: First Law of Thermodynamics.**
$$ \\Delta U = Q - W $$
$$ \\Delta U = 840 \\text{ J} - (-500 \\text{ J}) $$
$$ \\Delta U = 840 + 500 = 1340 \\text{ J} $$

**Result:** 1340 J

questions.stem: When $$ 260 \\text{ J} $$ of heat is supplied to a $$ 100 \\text{ g} $$ of metal block, its temperature increases from $$ 40^\\circ\\text{C} $$ to $$ 60^\\circ\\text{C} $$. The specific heat capacity of the metal block, in $$ \\text{J/kg }^\\circ\\text{C} $$, is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify given values.**
$$ Q = 260 \\text{ J} $$, $$ m = 100 \\text{ g} = 0.1 \\text{ kg} $$, $$ \\Delta T = 60 - 40 = 20^\\circ\\text{C} $$

**Step 2: Use the specific heat formula.**
$$ Q = mc\\Delta T $$

**Step 3: Solve for specific heat ($$ c $$).**
$$ 260 = 0.1 \\times c \\times 20 $$
$$ 260 = 2c $$
$$ c = \\frac{260}{2} = 130 \\text{ J/kg }^\\circ\\text{C} $$

**Result:** 130 J/kg °C

questions.stem: When a positively charged glass rod is brought near a bulb of a positively charged electroscope, the leaves of the electroscope
explanation_steps: The electroscope is already positively charged (leaves are apart). Bringing another positive charge near the bulb repels more positive charges down into the leaves, increasing the repulsive force between them and making them **diverge more**.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is **correct** concerning first condition of equilibrium?

options.A: The resultant force acting on a body is zero.
options.B: The vector sum of forces acting on an object is greater than one.
options.C: The sum of the clockwise moments about a point is equal to the sum of the counter clockwise moments.
options.D: The sum of the clockwise moments about a point is less than the sum of the counter clockwise moments.
options.E: The sum of moments of forces about a point in their plane is zero.

explanation_steps: The **first condition of equilibrium** states that for an object to be in translational equilibrium, the vector sum of all external forces acting on it must be zero ($$ ∑F = 0 $$). Statement C describes the second condition of equilibrium.

questions.stem: A boat is traveling at $$ 14 \\text{ km/h} $$ upstream. The speed of the stream is $$ 2 \\text{ km/h} $$. The velocity of the boat relative to the fixed reference on the bank of the river is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Understand 'upstream'.**
Upstream means the boat is moving against the current. 

**Step 2: Apply relative velocity logic.**
Velocity relative to ground ($$ V_g $$) = Velocity of boat ($$ V_b $$) - Velocity of stream ($$ V_s $$).

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ V_g = 14 \\text{ km/h} - 2 \\text{ km/h} = 12 \\text{ km/h} $$

**Result:** 12 km/h

questions.stem: A cannon is fired with initial speed of $$ 300 \\text{ m/s} $$ at an angle of $$ 15^\\circ $$ above the horizontal following a parabolic path. Neglecting air resistance, the horizontal distance travelled (range) of the projectile, in metres, is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Formula for horizontal range ($$ R $$).**
$$ R = \\frac{u^2 \sin(2\theta)}{g} $$

**Step 2: Identify variables.**
$$ u = 300 \\text{ m/s} $$, $$ \theta = 15^\\circ $$, $$ 2\theta = 30^\\circ $$, $$ g = 10 \\text{ m/s}^2 $$

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ R = \\frac{300^2 \\times \sin 30^\\circ}{10} $$
$$ R = \\frac{90,000 \\times 0.5}{10} $$
$$ R = \\frac{45,000}{10} = 4,500 \\text{ m} $$

**Result:** 4,500 m

questions.stem: Two point electric charges of $$ 2 \mu\\text{C} $$ and $$ 3 \mu\\text{C} $$ are separated by a distance of $$ 6 \\text{ cm} $$ from their centre. The electric potential at a point midway between the two charges, in volts, is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify given values and constants.**
$$ q_1 = 2 \\times 10^{-6} \\text{ C} $$, $$ q_2 = 3 \\times 10^{-6} \\text{ C} $$
Total distance = $$ 6 \\text{ cm} = 0.06 \\text{ m} $$. Distance to midpoint ($$ r $$) = $$ 3 \\text{ cm} = 0.03 \\text{ m} $$.
$$ k = 9 \\times 10^9 \\text{ N}·\\text{m}^2/\\text{C}^2 $$

**Step 2: Calculate total potential ($$ V $$) at midpoint.**
$$ V = V_1 + V_2 = \\frac{kq_1}{r} + \\frac{kq_2}{r} = \\frac{k(q_1 + q_2)}{r} $$

**Step 3: Plug in values.**
$$ V = \\frac{9 \\times 10^9 \\times (2 \\times 10^{-6} + 3 \\times 10^{-6})}{0.03} $$
$$ V = \\frac{9 \\times 10^9 \\times 5 \\times 10^{-6}}{3 \\times 10^{-2}} $$
$$ V = 3 \\times 10^{11} \\times 5 \\times 10^{-6} = 15 \\times 10^5 = 1.5 \\times 10^6 \\text{ V} $$

**Result:** $$ 1.5 \\times 10^6 \\text{ V} $$

questions.stem: A clinical thermometer is designed to measure the body temperature of patients. Such a thermometer is
explanation_steps: Clinical thermometers typically use mercury because it has a high coefficient of expansion, does not stick to the glass, and is easily visible.

questions.stem: Which of the following is non-luminous source of light?
explanation_steps: A **luminous** object produces its own light (Sun, stars, lamps). A **non-luminous** object (like a mirror or the Moon) only reflects light from other sources.

questions.stem: If a man's face is $$ 25 \\text{ cm} $$ in front of a shaving mirror producing erect image $$ 1.5 $$ times the size of face, the focal length of the mirror would be
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify given values.**
Object distance ($$ u $$) = $$ 25 \\text{ cm} $$. Magnification ($$ m $$) = $$ +1.5 $$ (positive because the image is erect/virtual).

**Step 2: Use magnification formula ($$ m = -v/u $$).**
$$ 1.5 = \\frac{-v}{25} \implies v = -37.5 \\text{ cm} $$

**Step 3: Use mirror formula to find focal length ($$ f $$).**
$$ \\frac{1}{f} = \\frac{1}{u} + \\frac{1}{v} $$
$$ \\frac{1}{f} = \\frac{1}{25} + \\frac{1}{-37.5} = \\frac{1.5 - 1}{37.5} = \\frac{0.5}{37.5} $$
$$ f = \\frac{37.5}{0.5} = 75 \\text{ cm} $$

**Result:** 75 cm

questions.stem: In a certain office building there are $$ 20 \\text{ rooms} $$. Each room has two $$ 100 \\text{ W} $$ computers working $$ 10 \\text{ hours} $$ per day. If the cost of $$ 1 \\text{ kWh} $$ is $$ 2.50 \\text{ Nakfa} $$, the monthly running cost for the computers, in Nakfa, is (Take one month to be $$ 30 \\text{ days} $$)
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate total power.**
$$ 20 \\text{ rooms} \\times 2 \\text{ computers/room} = 40 \\text{ computers} $$
Total Power = $$ 40 \\times 100 \\text{ W} = 4,000 \\text{ W} = 4 \\text{ kW} $$

**Step 2: Calculate monthly energy consumption.**
Energy = $$ \\text{Power} \\times \\text{Time} \\times \\text{Days} $$
Energy = $$ 4 \\text{ kW} \\times 10 \\text{ h/day} \\times 30 \\text{ days} = 1,200 \\text{ kWh} $$

**Step 3: Calculate cost.**
Cost = $$ 1,200 \\text{ kWh} \\times 2.50 \\text{ Nakfa/kWh} = 3,000 \\text{ Nakfa} $$

**Result:** 3,000 Nakfa

questions.stem: Which of the following phenomena of light results in a mirage?
explanation_steps: A mirage is caused by **Total Internal Reflection** (TIR) occurring in layers of air with different temperatures (and thus different refractive indices) near the ground.

questions.stem: The equivalent resistance of two identical resistors connected in parallel is $$ 6 \\text{ }Ω $$. The equivalent resistance of the same resistors connected in series is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find individual resistance ($$ R $$).**
For two identical resistors in parallel: $$ R_p = R/2 $$.
$$ 6 = R/2 \implies R = 12 \\text{ }Ω $$ each.

**Step 2: Calculate series resistance ($$ R_s $$).**
For resistors in series: $$ R_s = R + R = 12 + 12 = 24 \\text{ }Ω $$.

**Result:** $$ 24 \\text{ }Ω $$

questions.stem: If both the applied voltage and the current in a complete circuit are doubled the resistance will be
explanation_steps: According to Ohm's Law ($$ R = V/I $$), if both $$ V $$ and $$ I $$ are doubled ($$ 2V/2I $$), the ratio remains the same. Thus, resistance is **unchanged**.

questions.stem: The total magnification of a telescope having an objective lens of focal length $$ 50 \\text{ cm} $$ and an eye-piece lens of focal length $$ 5 \\text{ cm} $$ is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Use the telescope magnification formula.**
$$ M = \\frac{f_{\\text{objective}}}{f_{\\text{eyepiece}}} $$

**Step 2: Plug in values.**
$$ M = \\frac{50 \\text{ cm}}{5 \\text{ cm}} = 10 $$

**Result:** 10

questions.stem: Which of the following forms an image whose size is always smaller than the object?
explanation_steps: A **convex mirror** always produces virtual, erect, and **diminished** (smaller) images, regardless of the object's distance.

questions.stem: Which of the following **is not** true about a compound microscope?

options.A: It consists of two converging lenses.
options.B: The focal length of the eyepiece lens is larger than that of the objective lens.
options.C: The final image seen is virtual.
options.D: The object is placed near the focal point of the eyepiece lens.
options.E: Its magnification is the product of the magnification of the objective lens and the eyepiece lens.

explanation_steps: In a compound microscope, the object is placed just outside the focal point of the **objective lens**, not the eyepiece. The eyepiece then acts as a simple magnifier to enlarge the real image produced by the objective.

questions.stem: The splitting of white light into its component colors is called
explanation_steps: Dispersion is the phenomenon where white light splits into its constituent spectrum of colors (ROYGBIV) when passing through a medium like a prism.

questions.stem: A sound wave has a frequency of $$ 3 \\text{ kHz} $$ and wavelength $$ 25 \\text{ cm} $$. How much time will it take to travel $$ 1.5 \\text{ km} $$?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Convert units.**
$f = 3000 \\text{ Hz}$, $\lambda = 0.25 \\text{ m}$, $d = 1500 \\text{ m}$.

**Step 2: Find the speed of sound ($$ v $$).**
$v = f \\times \lambda = 3000 \\times 0.25 = 750 \\text{ m/s}$.

**Step 3: Calculate time ($$ t $$).**
$t = d / v = 1500 / 750 = 2.0 \\text{ s}$.

**Result:** 2.0 s

questions.stem: Two long parallel conductors carry $$ 100 \\text{ A} $$. If the conductors are separated by $$ 20 \\text{ mm} $$, the force per meter of length of each conductor will be
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify given values.**
$I_1 = I_2 = 100 \\text{ A}$, $d = 20 \\text{ mm} = 0.02 \\text{ m}$, $\mu_0 = 4\\pi \\times 10^{-7} \\text{ T}·\\text{m/A}$.

**Step 2: Apply the force formula.**
$\\frac{F}{L} = \\frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\\pi d} = \\frac{(4\\pi \\times 10^{-7}) \\times 100 \\times 100}{2\\pi \\times 0.02}$

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$\\frac{F}{L} = \\frac{2 \\times 10^{-7} \\times 10,000}{0.02} = \\frac{2 \\times 10^{-3}}{0.02} = 0.1 \\text{ N/m}$.

**Result:** 0.1 N/m

questions.stem: A man standing in between two parallel cliffs, produces a sound. The first echo is heard from cliff-1 after $$ 2 \\text{ seconds} $$ and a second echo is heard from cliff-2, $$ 1 \\text{ second} $$ after the first echo is heard. If the speed of sound in air is $$ 340 \\text{ m/s} $$, the distance between the two cliffs is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find distance to Cliff 1.**
$t_1 = 2 \\text{ s} \implies d_1 = (v \\times t_1) / 2 = (340 \\times 2) / 2 = 340 \\text{ m}$.

**Step 2: Find distance to Cliff 2.**
$t_2 = 2 + 1 = 3 \\text{ s} \implies d_2 = (v \\times t_2) / 2 = (340 \\times 3) / 2 = 510 \\text{ m}$.

**Step 3: Total distance between cliffs.**
$D = d_1 + d_2 = 340 + 510 = 850 \\text{ m}$.

**Result:** 850 m

questions.stem: A drawing pin with a tip area of $$ 0.1 \\text{ mm}^2 $$ is pushed against a board with a force of $$ 30 \\text{ N} $$. The pressure exerted at the tip, in newton per square meter, is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Convert area to $$ m^2 $$.**
$A = 0.1 \\text{ mm}^2 = 0.1 \\times 10^{-6} \\text{ m}^2 = 10^{-7} \\text{ m}^2$.

**Step 2: Use pressure formula.**
$P = F / A = 30 / 10^{-7} = 30 \\times 10^7 = 3 \\times 10^8 \\text{ N/m}^2$.

**Result:** $3 \\times 10^8 \\text{ N/m}^2$

questions.stem: What is the intensity level of a sound whose intensity is $$ 1.0 \\times 10^{-10} \\text{ W/m}^2 $$? (The threshold of hearing intensity is $$ I_0 = 1.0 \\times 10^{-12} \\text{ W/m}^2 $$)
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Use the intensity level formula.**
$\beta = 10 \\log(I/I_0)$

**Step 2: Calculate.**
$\beta = 10 \\log(10^{-10} / 10^{-12}) = 10 \\log(10^2)$
$\beta = 10 \\times 2 = 20 \\text{ dB}$.

**Result:** 20 dB

questions.stem: A charged particle is moving on circular path with velocity $$ v $$ in a uniform magnetic field $$ B $$, if the velocity of the charged particle is doubled and strength of magnetic field is halved, then the radius becomes _______ times as large as the original radius.
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Formula for radius of circular path.**
$r = mv / qB$

**Step 2: Apply changes.**
New velocity $v' = 2v$, New magnetic field $B' = B/2$.

**Step 3: Calculate new radius.**
$r' = m(2v) / q(B/2) = 4 \\times (mv / qB) = 4r$.

**Result:** 4 times

explanation_steps: Light waves and radio waves are part of the electromagnetic spectrum. Sound waves and water waves are mechanical waves which require a medium to travel.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Formula for period ($$ T $$).**
$T = 1 / f$

**Step 2: Calculate.**
$T = 1 / 1000 = 0.001 \\text{ s}$.

questions.stem: The loudness of sound waves increases with increasing
explanation_steps: Loudness is primarily determined by the **amplitude** of the sound wave. Larger amplitude means more energy and a louder sound. Frequency determines pitch.

questions.stem: The working principle for the operation of Hydraulic jack is based on
explanation_steps: **Pascal's Principle** states that pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished to every portion of the fluid. Hydraulic jacks use this to multiply force.

questions.stem: A strong magnetic field is applied on a stationary electron. Then the electron

options.A: moves in the direction of the field.
options.C: moves perpendicular to the direction of the field.
options.D: moves opposite to the direction of the field.

explanation_steps: The magnetic force on a charge is given by $F = qvB \sin\theta$. Since the electron is **stationary** ($v = 0$), the magnetic force is zero, and the electron remains stationary.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **incorrect** about photon?

options.A: The energy of a photon is proportional to the frequency of the wave radiation.
options.B: The energy of a photon is independent of the intensity of radiation.
options.C: Each photon moves with a speed of $3 \\times 10^8 \\text{ m/s}$ in vacuum.
options.E: Photons are easily deflected by magnetic field.

explanation_steps: Photons are packets of electromagnetic energy and have **no electrical charge** (neutral). Therefore, they are NOT deflected by magnetic or electric fields.

questions.stem: Probability of backward scattering (i.e. the scattering of $\alpha$-particles at angles greater than $90^\\circ$) predicted by Thomson's model is

options.A: much more than predicted by Rutherford's model.
options.B: much less than predicted by Rutherford's model.
options.C: same as predicted by Rutherford's model.
options.D: slightly less than predicted by Rutherford's model.
options.E: slightly more than predicted by Rutherford's model.

explanation_steps: Thomson's 'plum pudding' model predicted that $\alpha$-particles would pass through the atom with very little deflection. Rutherford's discovery of the dense nucleus explained why some particles scattered at very large angles, which Thomson's model could not.

questions.stem: Two photons, each of energy $2.5 \\text{ eV}$, are simultaneously incident on a metal surface. If the work function of the metal is $4.5 \\text{ eV}$, then from the surface of the metal

options.A: only one electron will be emitted with energy $0.5 \\text{ eV}$.
options.B: only one electron will be emitted with energy $2 \\text{ eV}$.
options.C: two electrons will be emitted with energy $0.25 \\text{ eV}$.
options.D: more than two electrons will be emitted.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Check the condition for photoelectric emission.**
Emission only occurs if the energy of a **single** photon ($E$) is greater than or equal to the work function ($\Phi$).

**Step 2: Compare values.**
$E = 2.5 \\text{ eV}$
$\Phi = 4.5 \\text{ eV}$
Since $2.5 < 4.5$, no individual photon has enough energy to knock out an electron.

**Step 3: Consider simultaneous hits.**
Photoelectric effect is a one-to-one interaction. Two low-energy photons cannot combine their energy to eject one electron.

**Result:** No emission.

questions.stem:
1. A lorry traveling at a speed of $36 \\text{ km/h}$ along a straight level road is brought uniformly to rest in a distance of $40.0 \\text{ m}$. If the lorry's mass is $500 \\text{ kg}$, find:
(a) the acceleration of the lorry in $\\text{m/s}^2$.
(b) the braking force, $F$, of the lorry in newtons.
explanation_steps:
**Given:**
$u = 36 \\text{ km/h} = 10 \\text{ m/s}$
$v = 0 \\text{ m/s}$ (rest)
$s = 40 \\text{ m}$
$m = 500 \\text{ kg}$

**(a) Acceleration:**
Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$
$0^2 = 10^2 + 2(a)(40)$
$0 = 100 + 80a$
$80a = -100 \implies a = -1.25 \\text{ m/s}^2$

**(b) Force:**
$F = ma$
$F = 500 \\text{ kg} \\times 1.25 \\text{ m/s}^2 = 625 \\text{ N}$

questions.stem:
2. A cylinder closed off with a movable piston contains $100 \\text{ g}$ of steam at $100 ^\\circ\\text{C}$ with a volume of $200 \\text{ cm}^3$. The system is heated and its temperature rises to $120 ^\\circ\\text{C}$ as the steam expands to a volume of $230 \\text{ cm}^3$ at a constant pressure of $5 \\times 10^5 \\text{ Pa}$. Calculate
(a) the work done by the steam.
(b) the change in its internal energy.
explanation_steps:
**Given:**
$m = 100 \\text{ g} = 0.1 \\text{ kg}$
$V_1 = 200 \\text{ cm}^3 = 200 \\times 10^{-6} \\text{ m}^3$
$V_2 = 230 \\text{ cm}^3 = 230 \\times 10^{-6} \\text{ m}^3$
$P = 5 \\times 10^5 \\text{ Pa}$
$c_{steam} = 2.02 \\times 10^3 \\text{ J/kg·K}$ (from constants)
$\\Delta T = 120 - 100 = 20 \\text{ K}$

**(a) Work Done:**
$W = P \\times \\Delta V = P(V_2 - V_1)$
$W = 5 \\times 10^5 \\times (230 - 200) \\times 10^{-6}$
$W = 5 \\times 10^5 \\times 30 \\times 10^{-6} = 15 \\text{ J}$

**(b) Internal Energy Change:**
First, find heat added ($Q$):
$Q = mc\\Delta T = 0.1 \\times 2020 \\times 20 = 4040 \\text{ J}$
Using 1st Law: $\\Delta U = Q - W$
$\\Delta U = 4040 - 15 = 4025 \\text{ J}$

questions.stem:
3. A student in a laboratory stretches a spring $0.5 \\text{ m}$ from rest by exerting a force which increases uniformly from zero to $250 \\text{ N}$. Find the

(b) work done by the student in pulling the spring.
explanation_steps:
**Given:**
$x = 0.5 \\text{ m}$, $F_{max} = 250 \\text{ N}$

**(a) Spring Constant:**
$F = kx \implies k = F / x$
$k = 250 / 0.5 = 500 \\text{ N/m}$

**(b) Work Done:**
$W = \\frac{1}{2}kx^2$ OR $W = \\text{Average Force} \\times \\text{distance}$
$W = \\frac{1}{2}(500)(0.5)^2 = 250 \\times 0.25 = 62.5 \\text{ J}$
Alternative: $W = [(0 + 250) / 2] \\times 0.5 = 125 \\times 0.5 = 62.5 \\text{ J}$

questions.stem:
4. (a) The critical angle for light going from glass to air is found to be $30^\\circ$. Find the index of refraction of the medium.
(b) A converging lens with focal length of $50 \\text{ cm}$ forms a real image that is $2.5$ times as large as the object. Calculate the distance of the object from the lens.
explanation_steps:
**(a) Index of Refraction ($n$):**
Use $\sin C = 1/n$
$n = 1 / \sin 30^∘ = 1 / 0.5 = 2.0$

**(b) Object Distance ($u$):**
Given $f = 50 \\text{ cm}$, $M = 2.5$
Magnification $M = v / u \implies v = 2.5u$ (Real image, so $v$ is positive in lens equation)
Lens formula: $1/f = 1/u + 1/v$
$1/50 = 1/u + 1/2.5u$
$1/50 = (2.5 + 1) / 2.5u = 3.5 / 2.5u$
$2.5u = 50 \\times 3.5 = 175$
$u = 175 / 2.5 = 70 \\text{ cm}$

questions.stem:
5. (a) Calculate the energy of a photon whose wavelength is $1.32 \\times 10^{-10} \\text{ m}$.
(b) Ultraviolet radiation of $7.2 \\text{ eV}$ energy falls on an aluminum surface of $4.2 \\text{ eV}$ work function. Find the kinetic energy, in joules, of the fastest electrons emitted.
explanation_steps:

Einstein's equation: $K_{max} = E_{photon} - \Phi$
$K_{max} = 7.2 \\text{ eV} - 4.2 \\text{ eV} = 3.0 \\text{ eV}$

questions.stem: Which one of the following pair is **not** fundamental quantity?
explanation_steps:
Fundamental quantities are independent physical quantities (Length, Mass, Time, Temperature, Electric Current, Amount of Substance, Luminous Intensity). 

**Momentum** ($$ p = mv $$) and **Impulse** ($$ J = F\Delta t $$) are derived quantities because they are calculated from fundamental ones.

questions.stem: A particle with mass 4kg moves along x-axis with initial speed of 2m/s. An opposing force of 8N is applied for time of 2s. Find the final velocity?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find acceleration (a).**
Using Newton's Second Law ($$ F = ma $$). Since the force is opposing, it is negative.
$$ a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{-8N}{4kg} = -2m/s^2 $$

**Step 2: Find final velocity (v).**
Using kinematics formula:
$$ v = u + at $$
$$ v = 2m/s + (-2m/s^2)(2s) $$
$$ v = 2 - 4 = -2m/s $$

questions.stem: One gram of water having volume of $$ 1cm^3 $$ becomes $$ 1671cm^3 $$ of steam when boiled at constant pressure of 1atm. The workdone in joules to completely vaporize it is;
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify Given Values.**
Pressure $$ P = 1 \, atm = 1.013 \times 10^5 \, Pa $$
Initial volume $$ V_1 = 1 \, cm^3 = 1 \times 10^{-6} \, m^3 $$
Final volume $$ V_2 = 1671 \, cm^3 = 1671 \times 10^{-6} \, m^3 $$

**Step 2: Calculate Change in Volume ($$ \Delta V $$).**
$$ \Delta V = V_2 - V_1 = 1670 \, cm^3 = 1670 \times 10^{-6} \, m^3 $$

**Step 3: Calculate Work Done ($$ W $$).**
$$ W = P \Delta V $$
$$ W = (1.013 \times 10^5) \times (1670 \times 10^{-6}) $$
$$ W \approx 169.17 \, J $$
Rounding gives 169J.

questions.stem: An object 4cm tall is 15cm in front of a lens of power 4D. The height of the image in cm is;
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find focal length (f).**
$$ f = \frac{1}{P} = \frac{1}{4} = 0.25m = 25cm $$.

**Step 2: Use lens formula to find image distance (v).**
$$ \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} $$ (using real-is-positive convention, $$ u=15, f=25 $$ for convex lens).
$$ \frac{1}{25} = \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{15} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{25} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{3+5}{75} = \frac{8}{75} $$
$$ v = 9.375 cm $$ (Wait, standard sign convention: $$ 1/v - 1/u = 1/f $$, $$ u = -15, f = +25 $$).
$$ 1/v = 1/25 + 1/(-15) = -2/75 \Rightarrow v = -37.5 cm $$.

**Step 3: Calculate magnification (m) and height (hi).**
$$ m = |\frac{v}{u}| = |\frac{-37.5}{-15}| = 2.5 $$
$$ h_i = m \times h_o = 2.5 \times 4 = 10 cm $$.

questions.stem: The number of significant figures of the resultant $$ 3.7m + 13.07m + 0.311m $$ is __________.
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Perform the addition.**
$$ 3.7 + 13.07 + 0.311 = 17.081 $$

**Step 2: Apply the rule for addition/subtraction.**
The result must be rounded to the least number of decimal places in the data. 
- 3.7 has 1 decimal place.
- 13.07 has 2 decimal places.
- 0.311 has 3 decimal places.

**Step 3: Rounding.**
Round 17.081 to 1 decimal place: **17.1**.

**Step 4: Count significant figures.**
17.1 has **3** significant figures.

questions.stem:
A truck covers 60m in 4s while smoothly slowing down to final speed of 2m/s. Find:
A) Truck’s initial speed
B) Truck's acceleration
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find Initial Speed (u).**
Using the formula for displacement with constant acceleration:
$$ s = \frac{u + v}{2}t $$
$$ 60 = \frac{u + 2}{2} \times 4 $$
$$ 60 = 2(u + 2) $$
$$ 30 = u + 2 \Rightarrow u = 28 \, m/s $$

**Step 2: Find Acceleration (a).**
Using the first equation of motion:
$$ v = u + at $$
$$ 2 = 28 + a(4) $$
$$ -26 = 4a \Rightarrow a = -6.5 \, m/s^2 $$

questions.stem: The dimensional formula for efficiency is;
explanation_steps:
Efficiency ($$ \eta $$) is defined as the ratio of Output Work to Input Work (or Power out to Power in). 

**Formula:** 
$$ \eta = \frac{W_{out}}{W_{in}} $$

Since it is a ratio of two identical physical quantities (Work/Work), it is dimensionless. Its dimensional formula is $$ M^0 L^0 T^0 $$. None of the given options match.

questions.stem: A man of mass 40kg climbs a wall 2m high, the work done due to gravity is;

questions.stem: Which one of the following is **false** about electrical force?

options.A: Force is directly proportional to the product of charges.
options.B: Ratio of gravitational to electrical force is $$ 10^{40} $$.
options.C: Force is inversely proportional to the square of the separation between the charges.
options.D: Electrical force is either attractive or repulsive.

explanation_steps:
Coulomb's Law states $$ F_e = k \frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2} $$. 
- A and C are true according to the formula.
- D is true because like charges repel and unlike charges attract.
- B is **false** because the electrical force is much stronger than the gravitational force. The ratio of Gravitational Force to Electrical Force ($$ F_g/F_e $$) is approximately $$ 10^{-40} $$, not $$ 10^{40} $$.

questions.stem: Inertia of a body depends on ___________ of an object.
explanation_steps: Inertia is the inherent property of an object to resist changes in its state of motion. The quantitative measure of inertia is **mass**. The more mass an object has, the greater its inertia.

questions.stem:
From the given figure:
A) Find workdone from x = 0 to x = 8m
B) Find workdone from x = 0 to x = 12m

![Work-Distance Graph](file:///android_asset/exam_images/physics_model_2024_2025_q52_1.webp)
explanation_steps:
Work done is equal to the area under the Force-Distance graph.

**Part A (0 to 8m):**
This is a triangle with base 8m and height 6N.
$$ Area = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = 0.5 \times 8 \times 6 = 24 \, J $$

**Part B (0 to 12m):**
Total work = Area (0 to 8m) + Area (8 to 12m).
The area from 8 to 12m is a triangle below the x-axis (negative work).
$$ Area_{8-12} = 0.5 \times (12 - 8) \times (-3) = 0.5 \times 4 \times -3 = -6 \, J $$
$$ Total \, Work = 24 + (-6) = 18 \, J $$

questions.stem: In a given system the sum of all energies of the molecules is called;

questions.stem:
Determine the point from the smaller charge in which the total electric field is zero.

![Charges Diagram](file:///android_asset/exam_images/physics_model_2024_2025_q23_1.webp)
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Analyze the charges.**
$$ q_1 = 25 \mu C $$ (smaller), $$ q_2 = -100 \mu C $$. Since they have opposite signs, the zero field point is outside the charges, closer to the smaller one.

**Step 2: Use the formula for distance (x) from the smaller charge.**
$$ x = \frac{d}{\sqrt{q_2/q_1} - 1} $$

**Step 3: Calculation.**
$$ x = \frac{4 \, m}{\sqrt{100/25} - 1} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{4} - 1} = \frac{4}{2 - 1} = 4 \, m $$
Since the smaller charge is on the left, the point is 4m (or 4cm if the unit in diagram was cm) to the left of the $$ 25 \mu C $$ charge.

questions.stem: If two long parallel wires 1m apart carry the same current and the force per unit length is $$ 2 \times 10^{-7} N/m $$, the current in each wire is;
explanation_steps:
**Formula:**
$$ \frac{F}{L} = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi r} $$

**Given:**
$$ F/L = 2 \times 10^{-7} $$, $$ r = 1m $$, $$ I_1 = I_2 = I $$, $$ \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} $$

**Calculation:**
$$ 2 \times 10^{-7} = \frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times I^2}{2\pi \times 1} $$
$$ 2 \times 10^{-7} = 2 \times 10^{-7} \times I^2 $$
$$ I^2 = 1 \Rightarrow I = 1A $$.

questions.stem: In projectile motion thrown at an angle the velocity at maximum height is _________.
explanation_steps: At the maximum height of a projectile's path, the vertical component of velocity ($$ v_y $$) becomes zero. However, the horizontal component ($$ v_x $$) remains constant throughout the flight (ignoring air resistance). Thus, the velocity at max height is exactly its horizontal component: $$ v = u \cos \theta $$.

questions.stem:
From the given circuit find:
A) equivalent resistance
B) power in 2Ω resistor

![Circuit Diagram](file:///android_asset/exam_images/physics_model_2024_2025_q53_1.webp)
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find Parallel Resistance (Rp).**
The resistors 6Ω, 3Ω, and 2Ω are in parallel.
$$ \frac{1}{R_p} = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1+2+3}{6} = \frac{6}{6} = 1 \, \Omega $$
$$ R_p = 1 \, \Omega $$

**Step 2: Find Total Equivalent Resistance (Req).**
Rp is in series with the 4Ω resistor.
$$ R_{eq} = 1 + 4 = 5 \, \Omega $$

**Step 3: Find Total Current (I).**
$$ I = \frac{V}{R_{eq}} = \frac{25V}{5\Omega} = 5 \, A $$

**Step 4: Find Power in 2Ω resistor.**
Voltage across the parallel part ($$ V_p $$) is $$ I \times R_p = 5A \times 1\Omega = 5V $$.
Since they are in parallel, the 2Ω resistor also has 5V across it.
$$ P = \frac{V^2}{R} = \frac{5^2}{2} = \frac{25}{2} = 12.5 \, W $$

questions.stem: An object initially moving at speed of 15m/s accelerates uniformly for 5s and reaches to final speed of 45m/s, the acceleration of the object in m/s²:
explanation_steps:
**Given:** 
Initial velocity $$ u = 15 \, m/s $$ 
Final velocity $$ v = 45 \, m/s $$ 
Time $$ t = 5 \, s $$ 

**Formula:** 
$$ a = \frac{v - u}{t} $$ 

**Calculation:** 
$$ a = \frac{45 - 15}{5} = \frac{30}{5} = 6 \, m/s^2 $$

questions.stem: A spring has a limit constant of 20N/m. The amount of work done to stretch it 0.40m from its equilibrium position is;
explanation_steps:
**Given:**
Spring constant $$ k = 20N/m $$, extension $$ x = 0.40m $$

**Formula:**
Work done on a spring (Elastic Potential Energy):
$$ W = \frac{1}{2}kx^2 $$

**Calculation:**

$$ W = 10 \times 0.16 = 1.6J $$

questions.stem: A resistor connected to a potential difference of 9v draws a current of 0.3A. The electrical power that the resistor uses in 1.5hr is;
explanation_steps:
**Given:**
Voltage $$ V = 9 \, V $$
Current $$ I = 0.3 \, A $$

**Formula:**
Power $$ P = V \times I $$

**Calculation:**
$$ P = 9 \times 0.3 = 2.7 \, W $$
Note: Power is independent of time. If the question asked for Energy, we would multiply by 1.5hr.

questions.stem: Two coils have a mutual inductance of 1.25H. Find the average electromotive force in the second coil if current in the primary is build up to 10A in 0.025s after circuit is closed?
explanation_steps:
**Formula:**
$$ \epsilon = -M \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} $$

**Given:**
$$ M = 1.25H $$, $$ \Delta I = 10A - 0A = 10A $$, $$ \Delta t = 0.025s $$

**Calculation:**
$$ \epsilon = -1.25 \times \frac{10}{0.025} $$
$$ \epsilon = -1.25 \times 400 = -500V $$.

questions.stem: _____________ is defined as the amount of heat necessary to raise the temperature of 1g of water by $$ 1^\circ C $$.
explanation_steps: One **calorie** (cal) is the energy needed to raise the temperature of 1 gram of water by 1 degree Celsius. In SI units, 1 calorie is approximately 4.184 Joules.

questions.stem:
Ray of light travelling with frequency of $$ 10^{15} \, Hz $$ in air strikes a glass surface (n=1.2) at $$ 53^\circ $$ with the surface. 
A) What is the angle of refraction?
B) What is the wavelength of the light in glass?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find Angle of Incidence (i).**
The angle with the surface is $$ 53^\circ $$, so the angle with the normal is:
$$ i = 90^\circ - 53^\circ = 37^\circ $$

**Step 2: Find Angle of Refraction (r) using Snell's Law.**
$$ n_1 \sin i = n_2 \sin r $$
$$ 1 \times \sin 37^\circ = 1.2 \times \sin r $$
$$ 0.6 = 1.2 \sin r \Rightarrow \sin r = 0.5 \Rightarrow r = 30^\circ $$

**Step 3: Find Wavelength in glass ($$ \lambda_g $$).**
Speed in glass $$ v = \frac{c}{n} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{1.2} = 2.5 \times 10^8 \, m/s $$
$$ \lambda_g = \frac{v}{f} = \frac{2.5 \times 10^8}{10^{15}} = 2.5 \times 10^{-7} \, m = 250 \, nm $$

questions.stem: One of the following is **true** statement about linear motion with constant velocity;

options.A: Distance is linear function of time.
options.B: Velocity is quadratic function of time.
options.C: Distance is quadratic function of time.
options.E: Acceleration is linear function of time.

explanation_steps:
In linear motion with constant velocity ($$ v $$): 
1. Acceleration is zero ($$ a = 0 $$). 
2. Velocity is constant (not a function of time). 
3. Distance ($$ s $$) is given by $$ s = vt + s_0 $$. 

Since $$ s $$ depends on $$ t $$ to the power of 1, distance is a **linear function** of time.

questions.stem: A ball is kicked from the ground with initial speed of 40m/s at angle of $$ 30^\circ $$ with horizontal surface. The velocity of the ball when it hits the ground is;
explanation_steps: In projectile motion (neglecting air resistance), the speed at which an object is launched from the ground is equal to the speed at which it returns to the same horizontal level. Only the direction changes, but the magnitude (speed) remains the same.

questions.stem: The unit volt per meter is the same as:
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Break down Volt.**
$$ 1 \, V = 1 \, J/C $$

**Step 2: Break down Joule.**
$$ 1 \, J = 1 \, N \cdot m $$

**Step 3: Combine.**
$$ V/m = (J/C)/m = (N \cdot m / C) / m = N/C $$
Both $$ V/m $$ and $$ N/C $$ are units for Electric Field Intensity.

questions.stem: A step up transformer operates on 110v line and supplies load with 2A. The ratio of primary coil to secondary coil respectively is 1:25. Power output is;
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find secondary voltage (Vs).**
$$ \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} \Rightarrow V_s = 110 \times \frac{25}{1} = 2750V $$.

**Step 2: Calculate Power output (Ps).**
$$ P_s = V_s \times I_s = 2750V \times 2A = 5500W $$
$$ P_s = 5.5 KW $$.

questions.stem: The centre of reflecting surface of spherical mirror is called ___________.
explanation_steps: The geometric center of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror (concave or convex) is called the **Pole** (P).

questions.stem:
A) What Energy of light would have to fall on sodium with workfunction of 3eV to emit electrons with maximum speed of $$ 10^6 \, m/s $$?
B) Find the frequency of incident light?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate Max Kinetic Energy ($$ K_{max} $$) in Joules.**
$$ K_{max} = \frac{1}{2} m v^2 = 0.5 \times (9 \times 10^{-31} \, kg) \times (10^6 \, m/s)^2 $$
$$ K_{max} = 4.5 \times 10^{-19} \, J $$

**Step 2: Convert $$ K_{max} $$ to eV.**
$$ K_{max} (eV) = \frac{4.5 \times 10^{-19}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}} = 2.8125 \, eV $$

**Step 3: Find Total Photon Energy (E).**
$$ E = \Phi + K_{max} = 3 \, eV + 2.8125 \, eV = 5.8125 \, eV $$

**Step 4: Find Frequency (f).**
$$ E = 5.8125 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, J = 9.3 \times 10^{-19} \, J $$
$$ f = \frac{E}{h} = \frac{9.3 \times 10^{-19}}{6.63 \times 10^{-34}} \approx 1.4 \times 10^{15} \, Hz $$

questions.stem: A book is at rest on a table. What is the reaction force on the book?

options.A: The force exerted by table on earth.
options.B: The force exerted by earth on table.
options.C: The force exerted by table on the book.

explanation_steps: When a book is at rest on a table, the earth pulls the book down (Weight). To stay at rest, the table must push the book upward with an equal force. This upward force exerted by the surface is called the **Normal Force** or the reaction of the table on the book.

questions.stem: Two cars A and B are moving in opposite direction with velocities of 40km/hr and 50km/hr respectively. The relative velocity of car A with respect to car B is:
explanation_steps:
**Formula:**
$$ v_{AB} = v_A - v_B $$

**Calculation:**
Since they move in opposite directions, if we take car A's direction as positive (+40), car B's direction is negative (-50).
$$ v_{AB} = 40 - (-50) = 40 + 50 = 90km/hr $$

questions.stem: Identify the **false** statement about image formation by a plane mirror;

options.B: Image is real, inverted and diminished.
options.D: Distance of object and distance of image are equal.

explanation_steps:
A plane mirror always forms an image that is:
1. Virtual (cannot be projected on a screen).
2. Upright (erect).
3. Same size as the object (not diminished).
4. Laterally inverted (left appears right).
5. Same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front.
Therefore, statement B is **false**.

questions.stem: Which of the following is **incorrect** statement?

options.A: Light refracts as it changes medium
options.B: Speed of light is different in different media
options.C: Speed of light in medium is less than speed of light in vacuum
options.D: A medium having higher refractive index allows light to travel faster

explanation_steps: Statement D is incorrect. The refractive index ($$ n $$) is defined as $$ n = c/v $$. Therefore, $$ v = c/n $$. As the refractive index increases, the speed of light in that medium **decreases**. Light travels slower in denser media.

questions.stem: __________ states that ‘’induced electro-motive force in a circuit is equal to the time rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit.’’
explanation_steps: **Faraday's Law** states that the magnitude of the induced EMF in a conductor is proportional to the rate at which the magnetic flux through the circuit changes over time ($$ \epsilon = -N \frac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} $$).

questions.stem:
A block of given mass is pushed & moves on horizontal surface as shown in the given figure. If coefficient of kinetic friction between block and the surface is 0.25, acceleration of the block in m/s² is;

![Diagram](file:///android_asset/exam_images/physics_model_2024_2025_q7_1.webp)
explanation_steps:
**Given:** 
$$ m = 10 \, kg $$, $$ F = 50 \, N $$, $$ \theta = 30^\circ $$, $$ \mu_k = 0.25 $$ 

**Step 1: Resolve Force components (Assuming a push as per common diagram logic):** 
$$ F_x = F \cos 30 = 50 \times 0.866 = 43.3 \, N $$ 
$$ F_y = F \sin 30 = 50 \times 0.5 = 25 \, N $$ (downward push) 

**Step 2: Find Normal Force (N):** 
$$ N = mg + F_y = (10 \times 10) + 25 = 125 \, N $$ 

**Step 3: Find Friction Force ($$ f_k $$):** 
$$ f_k = \mu_k N = 0.25 \times 125 = 31.25 \, N $$ 

**Step 4: Calculate Acceleration (a):** 
$$ F_{net} = F_x - f_k = 43.3 - 31.25 = 12.05 \, N $$ 
$$ a = \frac{F_{net}}{m} = \frac{12.05}{10} = 1.205 \, m/s^2 $$ 

*Note: Option C says 12.05, which matches the net force. There might be a typo in the question options (decimal place error).*

questions.stem:
Diving board 3m long is supported at a point 1m from one end. Diver weighing 680N stands at the other end. The diving board weights 400N. Find the force at the support point.

![Diving Board Diagram](file:///android_asset/exam_images/physics_model_2024_2025_q17_1.webp)
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify forces and positions.**
Let the left end be $$ x = 0 $$. 
Support force (F) is at $$ x = 1m $$. 
Weight of board (400N) is at center, $$ x = 1.5m $$. 
Diver (680N) is at the right end, $$ x = 3m $$.

**Step 2: Take moments about the left end ($$ x = 0 $$) to find F.**
$$ \sum \tau = 0 $$
$$ (F \times 1m) = (400N \times 1.5m) + (680N \times 3m) $$
$$ F = 600 + 2040 = 2640N $$

questions.stem: The angle of inclination between two mirrors if five images are formed is;
explanation_steps:
**Formula:**
The number of images ($$ n $$) formed by two mirrors at an angle $$ \theta $$ is:
$$ n = \frac{360}{\theta} - 1 $$

**Calculation:**
$$ 5 = \frac{360}{\theta} - 1 $$
$$ 6 = \frac{360}{\theta} $$
$$ \theta = \frac{360}{6} = 60^\circ $$

questions.stem: 11 successive crests are passing through a given point in one second. If the wavelength of the wave is 2m. Find the speed of the wave?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find frequency (f).**
11 successive crests mean there are 10 complete wave cycles ($$ n-1 $$). 
$$ f = 10 \text{ cycles} / 1 \text{ second} = 10 Hz $$.

**Step 2: Calculate wave speed (v).**
$$ v = f \lambda = 10 Hz \times 2m = 20 m/s $$.

questions.stem: Overlapping cyan and magenta filters produce ___________ colour.
explanation_steps:
This is subtractive color mixing:
- **Cyan** filter absorbs Red and transmits Green and Blue.
- **Magenta** filter absorbs Green and transmits Red and Blue.
When overlapped, Red is blocked by Cyan and Green is blocked by Magenta. Only **Blue** is transmitted by both.

questions.stem: Man of 50kg stands on an elevator of mass 70kg. The elevator accelerates upward at 3m/s². Find the tension in the string?
explanation_steps:
**Given:** 
Mass of man $$ m_1 = 50 \, kg $$ 
Mass of elevator $$ m_2 = 70 \, kg $$ 
Total mass $$ M = 50 + 70 = 120 \, kg $$ 
Acceleration $$ a = 3 \, m/s^2 $$ (upward) 

**Formula:** 
For upward acceleration: $$ T - Mg = Ma $$ 
$$ T = M(g + a) $$ 

**Calculation:** 
$$ T = 120 \times (10 + 3) $$ 
$$ T = 120 \times 13 = 1560 \, N $$

questions.stem: The transfer of energy across the boundary of a system due to temperature difference between the system and its surrounding is referred as;
explanation_steps: **Heat** is defined specifically as the energy in transit (transferring) from one body to another due to a temperature gradient.

questions.stem: In concave mirror no image is formed when an object is placed at;
explanation_steps: When an object is placed at the **Principal Focus (F)** of a concave mirror, the reflected rays are parallel to each other. Parallel rays meet at infinity, so no distinct image is formed at a finite distance.

questions.stem: Frequency arrangement order for electromagnetic spectrum in ascending order is;

options.A: Infrared, radio wave, microwave, Visible light, x-ray, UV light, gamma ray
options.B: Gamma, x-ray, visible, UV light, infrared, microwave, radio wave
options.C: Radio wave, microwave, infrared, visible, UV light, x-ray, gamma ray
options.D: Gamma, visible, x-ray, UV light, infrared, radio wave, microwave

explanation_steps:
Ascending order means from lowest frequency to highest frequency. The correct order is:
Radio waves (lowest f) < Microwaves < Infrared < Visible light < Ultraviolet < X-rays < Gamma rays (highest f).

questions.stem: When a sound wave travels from one medium to another _________ remains unchanged.
explanation_steps: When any wave (sound or light) moves from one medium to another, its speed and wavelength change, but its **frequency** remains constant because it is determined by the source of the wave.

questions.stem: A ball of mass 0.10kg moving with speed of 2m/s hits a wall and bounced back with the same speed. The change in KE is:
explanation_steps:
Kinetic Energy ($$ KE $$) is a scalar quantity given by: 
$$ KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 $$ 

Initial $$ KE = \frac{1}{2}(0.10)(2)^2 = 0.2 \, J $$ 
Final $$ KE = \frac{1}{2}(0.10)(2)^2 = 0.2 \, J $$ 

**Change in KE:** 
$$ \Delta KE = KE_{final} - KE_{initial} = 0.2 - 0.2 = 0 \, J $$

questions.stem: Gas molecules stop their motion at a temperature of;
explanation_steps: Absolute zero is the temperature at which molecular motion reaches its minimum (theoretically stops). This occurs at **0 Kelvin** or **-273.15 Celsius**. Both A and B are correct representations of this point.

questions.stem: A glass of refracting angle of $$ 60^\circ $$ gives minimum deviation of $$ 30^\circ $$. The refractive index of the glass is;
explanation_steps:
**Formula for Prism:**
$$ n = \frac{\sin(\frac{A + D_m}{2})}{\sin(\frac{A}{2})} $$
Where $$ A = 60^\circ $$ and $$ D_m = 30^\circ $$.

**Calculation:**
$$ n = \frac{\sin(\frac{60 + 30}{2})}{\sin(\frac{60}{2})} = \frac{\sin 45}{\sin 30} $$
$$ n = \frac{0.707}{0.5} = 1.414 $$
Refractive index is 1.41.

questions.stem: How high does a mercury in a barometer stand when atmospheric pressure is 98.6Kpa?
explanation_steps:
**Formula:**
$$ P = \rho g h $$

**Given:**
$$ P = 98.6 \times 10^3 Pa $$, $$ \rho_{Hg} = 13.6 \times 10^3 kg/m^3 $$, $$ g = 10 m/s^2 $$

**Calculation:**
$$ 98.6 \times 10^3 = (13.6 \times 10^3) \times 10 \times h $$
$$ 98.6 = 136 \times h $$
$$ h = 98.6 / 136 \approx 0.725 m = 725 mm $$.

questions.stem: ______ is a device that converts electrical energy to mechanical energy.
explanation_steps: An **Electric Motor** uses electromagnetic induction to turn electrical current into rotational motion (mechanical energy). A generator does the exact opposite.

questions.stem: A boy throws a ball straight up and the ball returns after 3s. The magnitude of the initial velocity and maximum height respectively are;
explanation_steps:
**Given:** 
Total time of flight $$ T = 3 \, s $$ 
Time to reach max height $$ t = T/2 = 1.5 \, s $$ 

**Step 1: Find Initial Velocity (u):** 
At max height, $$ v = 0 $$. 
$$ v = u - gt \Rightarrow 0 = u - (10)(1.5) \Rightarrow u = 15 \, m/s $$ 

**Step 2: Find Max Height (H):** 
$$ H = \frac{u^2}{2g} = \frac{15^2}{2(10)} = \frac{225}{20} = 11.25 \, m $$

questions.stem: Alcohol **cannot** be used for temp higher than $$ 78^\circ C $$ because alcohol has;
explanation_steps: Alcohol (ethanol) has a boiling point of approximately $$ 78^\circ C $$. If used in a thermometer for temperatures higher than this, it would turn into vapor, making it useless for measuring liquid temperature.

questions.stem: A person with hypermetropia **cannot** read instructions located at a distance of;
explanation_steps: **Hypermetropia** (farsightedness) is a vision defect where a person can see distant objects clearly but cannot focus on near objects. The near point is further than the normal 25cm. Therefore, they cannot read things located **less than 25cm** (or even at 25cm) clearly.

questions.stem: The threshold wavelength of potassium is 620nm. The work function in eV is ;
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate work function in Joules.**
$$ \Phi = \frac{hc}{\lambda_0} = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{620 \times 10^{-9}} $$
$$ \Phi \approx 3.2 \times 10^{-19} J $$.

**Step 2: Convert to eV.**
$$ \Phi (eV) = \frac{3.2 \times 10^{-19} J}{1.6 \times 10^{-19} J/eV} = 2 eV $$.

questions.stem: The spectrum with missing frequency is called ______________.
explanation_steps: An **Absorption Spectrum** is formed when light passes through a cool gas. The gas atoms absorb specific frequencies, leaving dark lines (missing frequencies) in the continuous spectrum.

questions.stem: Which of the following sets of physical quantities are all fundamental quantities?

options.E: mass, length, amount of substance, density

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Define Fundamental Quantities.**
Fundamental quantities are basic physical quantities that do not depend on any other quantities for their measurement. There are 7 SI base quantities: Mass, Length, Time, Temperature, Electric Current, Amount of Substance, and Luminous Intensity.

**Step 2: Evaluate the options.**
*   **A:** Weight is a derived quantity (Force).
*   **B:** Area, Volume, and Density are derived.
*   **C:** Mass, Length, Time, and Electric Current are all fundamental. (Correct)
*   **D:** All these are derived from mass, length, and time.
*   **E:** Density is derived (Mass/Volume).

questions.stem: The prefix mega represents
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Recall Metric Prefixes.**
Metric prefixes are used to express large or small quantities in powers of 10.
*   Micro ($$ \mu $$) = $$ 10^{-6} $$
*   Milli (m) = $$ 10^{-3} $$
*   Kilo (k) = $$ 10^3 $$
*   Mega (M) = $$ 10^6 $$
*   Giga (G) = $$ 10^9 $$

**Step 2: Identify Mega.**
Mega represents one million, which is $$ 10^6 $$.

questions.stem: Taking into account the significant figures, what is the value of the sum $$ 2.0347\\text{ cm} + 15.7\\text{ cm} $$?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Perform the addition.**
$$ 2.0347 + 15.7 = 17.7347 $$

**Step 2: Apply the rule for addition/subtraction.**
When adding or subtracting, the final answer should have the same number of decimal places as the number with the fewest decimal places.
*   $$ 2.0347 $$ has 4 decimal places.
*   $$ 15.7 $$ has 1 decimal place (least precise).

**Step 3: Round the result.**
We must round $$ 17.7347 $$ to 1 decimal place.
The result is $$ 17.7 \\text{ cm} $$.

questions.stem: An object has a constant acceleration of $$ 2.0\\text{ m/s}^2 $$ in the +x direction. That means the

options.A: distance of the object increases by 2 m/s every second.
options.B: displacement of the object increases by 2 m/s every second.
options.C: speed of the object is 2 m/s every second.
options.D: velocity of the object is 2 m/s every second.
options.E: velocity of the object increases by 2 m/s every second.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Define Acceleration.**
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. A constant acceleration of $$ 2.0\\text{ m/s}^2 $$ means that the velocity of the object changes by $$ 2.0\\text{ m/s} $$ for every second that passes.

**Step 2: Match with options.**
*   Option E correctly states that the velocity increases by $$ 2\\text{ m/s} $$ every second.

questions.stem: A car starts from rest and accelerates at a steady rate of $$ 6.00\\text{ m/s}^2 $$. How far does it travel in the first $$ 3.00\\text{ s} $$?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify Given Values.**
*   Initial velocity ($$ u $$) = 0 m/s (starts from rest)
*   Acceleration ($$ a $$) = $$ 6.00\\text{ m/s}^2 $$
*   Time ($$ t $$) = $$ 3.00\\text{ s} $$

**Step 2: Choose the Kinematic Equation.**
To find distance ($$ s $$), use: $$ s = ut + \\frac{1}{2}at^2 $$

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ s = (0)(3) + \\frac{1}{2}(6.00)(3.00)^2 $$
$$ s = 0 + 3(9) $$
$$ s = 27.0\\text{ m} $$

questions.stem: A 10 kg rock and 20 kg rock are dropped from the same height and experience no significant air resistance. If it takes the 20 kg rock a time of 2 s to reach the ground, what time will it take the 10 kg rock to reach the ground?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Understand Free Fall.**
In a vacuum (or where air resistance is negligible), all objects fall with the same constant acceleration ($$ g \approx 10\\text{ m/s}^2 $$) regardless of their mass.

**Step 2: Conclusion.**
Since both rocks are dropped from the same height and air resistance is ignored, they will take the exact same amount of time to hit the ground. Therefore, the 10 kg rock will also take 2 s.

questions.stem: A body is thrown vertically upward from the ground. It reaches a maximum height of 125 m in 5 s. How much time, in seconds, will it take to reach the ground from the maximum height position?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Symmetry of Vertical Motion.**
In the absence of air resistance, the time taken to reach the maximum height from the ground is equal to the time taken to return to the ground from that maximum height.

**Step 2: Apply to the problem.**
If it took 5 s to reach the top, it will take exactly 5 s to fall back down from that top position to the ground.

questions.stem: A player catches a ball of 200 g moving with a speed of 25 m/s. If the time taken to complete the catch is 0.5 s, the force exerted, in newtons, on the player's hand is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Convert units.**
*   Mass ($$ m $$) = 200 g = $$ 0.2\\text{ kg} $$
*   Initial speed ($$ v_i $$) = 25 m/s
*   Final speed ($$ v_f $$) = 0 m/s (ball stops)
*   Time ($$ \\Delta t $$) = 0.5 s

**Step 2: Use Newton's Second Law in terms of momentum.**
$$ F = \\frac{\\Delta p}{\\Delta t} = \\frac{m(v_f - v_i)}{\\Delta t} $$

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ F = \\frac{0.2(0 - 25)}{0.5} = \\frac{-5}{0.5} = -10\\text{ N} $$
Magnitude of force is 10 N.

questions.stem: Which of the following **is not** an effect of a force acting on an object?

options.A: Change in shape of the object
options.B: Change in mass of the object
options.C: Change in size of the object
options.D: Change in velocity of the object
options.E: Change in direction of motion of the object

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Analyze effects of force.**
A force can change an object's:
- Shape or Size (e.g., squeezing a ball)
- Velocity (speeding up or slowing down)
- Direction of motion

**Step 2: Identify the outlier.**
Mass is an intrinsic property of an object (the amount of matter it contains). Applying a force to a rock does not change how much matter is inside the rock. Therefore, force does not change mass.

questions.stem: An object of mass 3 kg is sliding with a constant velocity of 4 m/s on a frictionless horizontal table. The force, in newtons, required to keep the object moving with the same velocity is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Understand Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia).**
An object in motion will remain in motion with a constant velocity unless acted upon by a net external force.

**Step 2: Apply to the frictionless case.**
Since the table is frictionless, there is no force opposing the motion. Therefore, no force is required to keep the object moving at a constant velocity. The net force required is zero.

questions.stem: Which of the following forces is a contact force?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Understand Force Categories.**
Forces are divided into two main types:
1. **Contact Forces:** Require physical touch (e.g., Friction, Tension, Normal force).
2. **Field Forces (Non-contact):** Act over a distance through a field (e.g., Gravity, Electricity, Magnetism).

**Step 2: Evaluate the options.**
Coulomb, Magnetic, Electrostatic, and Gravitational forces all act without touching. Only Frictional force requires two surfaces to be in physical contact.

questions.stem: A body of mass 10 kg is moved parallel to the ground through a distance of 2 m. The work done, in joules, against gravitational force is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Understand Work Done against Gravity.**
Work is done against gravity only when there is a vertical displacement (lifting an object up or lowering it down).

**Step 2: Analyze the motion.**
The object is moved *parallel* to the ground (horizontally). This means the vertical displacement ($$ h $$) is zero.

**Step 3: Calculate.**
Work against gravity = $$ mgh $$. Since $$ h = 0 $$, Work = $$ 10 \\times 10 \\times 0 = 0 \\text{ J} $$.
Also, the angle between the force of gravity (downward) and displacement (horizontal) is $$ 90^\\circ $$. Since $$\cos(90^\\circ) = 0 $$, work done is zero.

questions.stem: An object of weight 7 N is raised from a height of 2 m to a height of 8 m. The change in gravitational potential energy is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify Given Values.**
*   Weight ($$ W = mg $$) = 7 N
*   Initial height ($$ h_1 $$) = 2 m
*   Final height ($$ h_2 $$) = 8 m

**Step 2: Use the Formula for Change in Potential Energy.**
$$ \\Delta PE = mg(h_2 - h_1) = W \\times (h_2 - h_1) $$

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ \\Delta PE = 7 \\text{ N} \\times (8 \\text{ m} - 2 \\text{ m}) $$
$$ \\Delta PE = 7 \\times 6 = 42 \\text{ J} $$

questions.stem: If two bodies of different masses are projected at $$ 20^\\circ $$ and $$ 70^\\circ $$ with the same velocity, then

options.A: their maximum heights are the same.
options.C: their times of flight are the same.
options.D: the heavier object will have smaller time of flight.
options.E: the heavier object will have greater acceleration.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Understand Complementary Angles in Projectiles.**
For a projectile launched with a specific velocity, the range ($$ R $$) is the same for any two launch angles that add up to $$ 90^\\circ $$ (complementary angles).

**Step 2: Apply to the problem.**
The angles given are $$ 20^\\circ $$ and $$ 70^\\circ $$. 
$$ 20^\\circ + 70^\\circ = 90^\\circ $$.

**Step 3: Conclusion.**
Since the launch angles are complementary and the velocity is the same, their horizontal ranges will be identical.

questions.stem: If a projectile is launched at an angle of $$ 30^\\circ $$ with the horizontal, what is the vertical component of the initial velocity, in m/s, if the initial speed is 20 m/s?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify Given Values.**
*   Initial speed ($$ v $$) = 20 m/s
*   Angle ($$ \theta $$) = $$ 30^\\circ $$

**Step 2: Use Vector Resolution Formula.**
The vertical component ($$ v_y $$) is calculated as: $$ v_y = v \\cdot \sin(\theta) $$

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ v_y = 20 \\times \sin(30^\\circ) $$
We know $$ \sin(30^\\circ) = 0.5 $$
$$ v_y = 20 \\times 0.5 = 10 \\text{ m/s} $$

questions.stem: In a non-uniform circular motion the

options.A: speed is constant but the velocity is not.
options.B: velocity and the acceleration are perpendicular to each other.
options.C: acceleration is directed towards the center.
options.D: acceleration is perpendicular to the radius.
options.E: acceleration has both radial and tangential components.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Define Non-uniform Circular Motion.**
In non-uniform circular motion, an object moves in a circle but its **speed is changing**.

**Step 2: Analyze Acceleration.**
Because it's a circle, it must have **Radial (Centripetal) Acceleration** ($$ a_r $$) to change its direction.
Because the speed is changing, it must also have **Tangential Acceleration** ($$ a_t $$) to change the magnitude of velocity.

**Step 3: Conclusion.**
Therefore, the total acceleration is the vector sum of both radial and tangential components.

questions.stem: What is the value of absolute zero temperature on the Celsius Scale?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Define Absolute Zero.**
Absolute zero is the lowest possible temperature where all molecular motion stops. It is defined as 0 Kelvin (0 K).

**Step 2: Convert Kelvin to Celsius.**
The relationship is: $$ T(^\\circ\\text{C}) = T(\\text{K}) - 273.15 $$
$$ T(^\\circ\\text{C}) = 0 - 273.15 \approx -273^\\circ\\text{C} $$

questions.stem: The amount of heat necessary to raise the temperature of 1 g of water by $$ 1^\\circ\\text{C} $$, that is, from $$ 14.5^\\circ\\text{C} $$ to $$ 15.5^\\circ\\text{C} $$, is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Define the units of heat.**
- **Calorie:** The energy needed to raise 1 gram of water by $$ 1^\\circ\\text{C} $$.
- **Specific Heat:** The property of a substance (amount of heat per unit mass per degree).
- **Latent Heat:** Heat needed for a phase change without changing temperature.
- **BTU:** Heat needed to raise 1 pound of water by $$ 1^\\circ\\text{F} $$.

**Step 2: Conclusion.**
The definition perfectly matches the 'calorie'.

questions.stem: A faulty thermometer has its lower and upper fixed points marked as $$ 5^\\circ $$ and $$ 95^\\circ $$ respectively. The temperature of a body as measured by the thermometer is $$ 59^\\circ $$. The correct temperature of the body on a Celsius scale is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Understand the scaling relationship.**
For any thermometer, the ratio of (Reading - Lower Point) to (Upper Point - Lower Point) remains constant.

**Step 2: Set up the equation.**
Let $$ X $$ be the faulty reading and $$ C $$ be the correct Celsius reading.
$$ \\frac{X - L_X}{U_X - L_X} = \\frac{C - L_C}{U_C - L_C} $$

**Step 3: Plug in values.**
Faulty: $$ L_X = 5, U_X = 95, X = 59 $$
Celsius: $$ L_C = 0, U_C = 100 $$
$$ \\frac{59 - 5}{95 - 5} = \\frac{C - 0}{100 - 0} $$
$$ \\frac{54}{90} = \\frac{C}{100} $$
$$ 0.6 = \\frac{C}{100} $$
$$ C = 60^\\circ\\text{C} $$

questions.stem: A glass rod rubbed with silk acquires a charge of $$ -3.2 \\times 10^{-12} \\text{ C} $$. The number of electrons it has gained is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Recall the charge of a single electron.**
The elementary charge ($$ e $$) is approximately $$ 1.6 \\times 10^{-19} \\text{ C} $$.

**Step 2: Use the quantization of charge formula.**
$$ Q = ne $$, where $$ n $$ is the number of electrons and $$ Q $$ is total charge.
$$ n = \\frac{Q}{e} $$

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ n = \\frac{3.2 \\times 10^{-12}}{1.6 \\times 10^{-19}} $$
$$ n = 2.0 \\times 10^{-12 - (-19)} $$
$$ n = 2.0 \\times 10^7 $$

questions.stem: When $$ 240\\text{ J} $$ of work is done on a sample of confined helium gas, its internal energy increases by $$ 300\\text{ J} $$. How much heat is transferred between the gas and its environment?

options.A: $$ 540\\text{ J} $$ of heat flows into the gas.
options.B: $$ 60\\text{ J} $$ of heat flows into the gas.
options.C: $$ 540\\text{ J} $$ of heat flows out of the gas.
options.D: $$ 60\\text{ J} $$ of heat flows out of the gas.
options.E: No heat flows into or out of the gas.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: State the First Law of Thermodynamics.**
$$ \\Delta U = Q + W_{on} $$, where $$ \\Delta U $$ is the change in internal energy, $$ Q $$ is the heat added to the system, and $$ W_{on} $$ is the work done **on** the system.

**Step 2: Plug in the given values.**
*   $$ \\Delta U = +300\\text{ J} $$ (increase)
*   $$ W_{on} = +240\\text{ J} $$ (work done on the gas)

**Step 3: Solve for Q.**
$$ 300 = Q + 240 $$
$$ Q = 300 - 240 = +60\\text{ J} $$

**Step 4: Interpret the sign.**
Since $$ Q $$ is positive, $$ 60\\text{ J} $$ of heat flows **into** the gas.

questions.stem: Which of the following produces large electrostatic potential?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify the purpose of each device.**
- **Van de Graaff generator:** Specifically designed to build up very high static electric potentials (voltages).
- **Electric generator:** Produces electric current via electromagnetic induction.
- **Galvanometer:** Detects small electric currents.
- **Rheostat:** A variable resistor used to control current.
- **Electroscope:** Detects the presence of electric charge but doesn't produce high potential.

**Step 2: Conclusion.**
The Van de Graaff generator is the correct choice for producing large electrostatic potentials.

questions.stem: The electrostatic potential energy of two point charges $$ q_1 = -2\mu\\text{C} $$ and $$ q_2 = +2\mu\\text{C} $$ when separated by a distance of $$ 4\\text{ mm} $$ is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify Given Values and convert to SI units.**
*   $$ q_1 = -2 \\times 10^{-6}\\text{ C} $$
*   $$ q_2 = +2 \\times 10^{-6}\\text{ C} $$
*   $$ r = 4\\text{ mm} = 4 \\times 10^{-3}\\text{ m} $$
*   $$ k = 9 \\times 10^9\\text{ N}\\cdot\\text{m}^2/\\text{C}^2 $$

**Step 2: Use the Electrostatic Potential Energy formula.**
$$ U = k \\frac{q_1 q_2}{r} $$

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ U = (9 \\times 10^9) \\frac{(-2 \\times 10^{-6})(2 \\times 10^{-6})}{4 \\times 10^{-3}} $$
$$ U = (9 \\times 10^9) \\frac{-4 \\times 10^{-12}}{4 \\times 10^{-3}} $$
$$ U = 9 \\times (-1) \\times 10^{9-12+3} = -9 \\times 10^0 = -9\\text{ J} $$

questions.stem: A parallel combination consisting of two resistors A and B are connected across the terminals of a battery. The resistance of A is twice the resistance of B. If the current flowing through resistor A is $$ 0.4\\text{ A} $$ then the current flowing through resistor B is
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Understand Parallel Circuits.**
In a parallel circuit, the voltage ($$ V $$) across each resistor is the same.
$$ V_A = V_B $$

**Step 2: Use Ohm's Law ($$ V = IR $$).**
$$ I_A R_A = I_B R_B $$

**Step 3: Plug in the relationship between resistances.**
Given: $$ R_A = 2R_B $$ and $$ I_A = 0.4\\text{ A} $$.
$$ (0.4) \\times (2R_B) = I_B \\times R_B $$
$$ 0.8 R_B = I_B R_B $$

**Step 4: Solve for $$ I_B $$.**
$$ I_B = 0.8\\text{ A} $$

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements **is not** correct about reflection of light?

options.A: Laws of reflection are valid to regular reflection only.
options.B: Laws of reflection are valid to both regular and irregular reflections.
options.C: One of the laws of reflection states that angle of incidence is equal to angle of reflection.
options.D: Image is formed by the reflection of light from a smooth surface.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Evaluate the laws of reflection.**
The laws of reflection (Angle of Incidence = Angle of Reflection) apply at every single point where a light ray hits a surface, regardless of whether the surface is smooth (regular) or rough (irregular).

questions.stem: Which of the following statements **is correct**?

options.A: The image formed by a concave mirror is always real.
options.B: The image formed by a concave mirror is always virtual.
options.C: The image formed by a convex mirror is always virtual.
options.D: The image formed by a convex mirror can be real or virtual.
options.E: The image formed by a convex mirror is always magnified.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Analyze Convex Mirrors.**
Convex (diverging) mirrors always spread light rays apart. They can **only** produce images that are virtual, upright, and diminished (smaller), no matter where the object is placed.

**Step 2: Analyze Concave Mirrors.**
Concave (converging) mirrors can produce either real or virtual images depending on the object's position (Real if outside focus, virtual if inside focus).

**Step 3: Select the correct statement.**
Option C is the only absolute truth: Convex mirrors always produce virtual images.

questions.stem: Which position of the object will produce a magnified, virtual image, if a concave mirror of focal length $$ 15\\text{ cm} $$ is being used?
explanation_steps:

A concave mirror produces a **virtual and magnified** image only when the object is placed **inside the focal length** ($$ d_o < f $$).

**Step 2: Apply to the given focal length.**
Focal length ($$ f $$) = $$ 15\\text{ cm} $$.
Therefore, the object must be placed at a distance less than $$ 15\\text{ cm} $$.

**Step 3: Select the option.**
Only $$ 10\\text{ cm} $$ (Option A) is less than $$ 15\\text{ cm} $$.

questions.stem: When a ray of light passes from optically rarer medium to optically denser medium at an angle of incidence different from $$ 0^\\circ $$,

options.A: the frequency of the light changes.
options.B: its angle of refraction becomes less than its angle of incidence.
options.C: its speed in the second medium is greater than in the first medium.
options.D: it bends away from the normal line.

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Understand Refraction Rules.**
- **Rarer to Denser:** Light slows down and bends **towards** the normal. This makes the angle of refraction ($$ r $$) smaller than the angle of incidence ($$ i $$).
- **Denser to Rarer:** Light speeds up and bends away from the normal.

**Step 2: Evaluate Frequency.**
Frequency of light is determined by the source and **never changes** when passing from one medium to another.

**Step 3: Conclusion.**
Option B is correct: the angle of refraction is less than the angle of incidence.

questions.stem: The image formed by a camera is

options.C: real, inverted and the same size as the object.

explanation_steps:

A camera uses a convex (converging) lens to project an image onto a film or sensor. To capture a whole scene onto a small sensor, the image must be smaller than the actual object.

**Step 2: Characteristics of the image.**
- **Real:** It can be projected onto a surface (sensor).
- **Inverted:** Convex lenses form inverted real images.
- **Diminished:** It must be small to fit inside the camera.

**Step 3: Conclusion.**
The image is real, inverted, and diminished.

questions.stem: An object placed in front of a converging lens forms 0.25 times magnified image on a screen. The screen is placed at 120 cm from the object. The distances of the image and the object, in cm, are **respectively**

questions.stem: Magnetic flux is maximum when the magnetic field is ________ to the surface.
explanation_steps:

**Step 2: Analyze the formula.**

**Step 3: Determine maximum condition.**
Flux is maximum when the field lines are perpendicular to the surface because they fully penetrate the area. In this orientation, the angle with the normal is $$ 0^\\circ $$, and $$ \cos(0) = 1 $$.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements **is correct** about transformers?

options.A: A transformer is an electric device that is used to increase or decrease DC voltage.

options.C: Step-up transformer is a transformer in which secondary current is greater than primary current.

explanation_steps:

questions.stem: An electron is traveling perpendicular to a $$ 0.045\\text{ T} $$ in a circular path of radius $$ 1.5\\text{ mm} $$. The magnitude of momentum of the electron, in kgm/s, is

questions.stem: The interference of two waves of the same frequency but different amplitude moving out of phase is
explanation_steps:

questions.stem: What is the frequency, in Hz, of a microwave whose wave length is 2.50 cm?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify given values.**
- Wavelength ($$ \lambda $$) = 2.50 cm = $$ 0.025\\text{ m} $$

**Step 2: Use the wave equation.**
$$ c = f \\cdot \lambda \implies f = \\frac{c}{\lambda} $$
**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ f = \\frac{3 \\times 10^8}{0.025} = \\frac{3 \\times 10^8}{2.5 \\times 10^{-2}} $$
$$ f = 1.2 \\times 10^{8 - (-2)} = 1.2 \\times 10^{10}\\text{ Hz} $$.

questions.stem: Two sound waves with wavelengths $$ 5.0\\text{ m} $$ and $$ 5.5\\text{ m} $$, **respectively**, propagate in air with a velocity of $$ 330\\text{ m/s} $$. How many beats per second do they make?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate the frequency of each wave.**

- $$ f_1 = 330 / 5.0 = 66\\text{ Hz} $$
- $$ f_2 = 330 / 5.5 = 60\\text{ Hz} $$

**Step 2: Calculate the beat frequency.**
The beat frequency is the absolute difference between the two frequencies:
- $$ f_{beat} = |f_1 - f_2| = |66 - 60| = 6\\text{ Hz} $$.
So, they make 6 beats per second.

questions.stem: What is the maximum pressure exerted by a rectangular block of iron with dimensions $$ 0.20\\text{ m} \\times 0.10\\text{ m} \\times 0.05\\text{ m} $$ and density of $$ 8000\\text{ kg/m}^3 $$ when suitably placed on a surface?
explanation_steps:

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements **is correct** about hydrostatic pressure?

Option A correctly identifies density as a deciding factor.

questions.stem: In a hydraulic press, the radius of the larger and smaller pistons are $$ 10\\text{ cm} $$ and $$ 5\\text{ cm} $$, **respectively**. If a force of $$ 800\\text{ N} $$ is applied to the smaller piston, then the force on the larger piston will be
explanation_steps:

questions.stem: The maximum kinetic energy of an electron ejected from a sodium surface of work function, $$ \phi_o = 3.65 \\times 10^{-19}\\text{ J} $$, is $$ 1.32 \\times 10^{-19}\\text{ J} $$. What is the wave length of the illuminated light?
explanation_steps:

Energy of photon ($$ E $$) = Work function ($$ \phi $$) + Max Kinetic Energy ($$ K_{max} $$)

Using $$ hc \approx 1.989 \\times 10^{-25} \\text{ J}\\cdot\\text{m} $$
